task.description:
Design a fix for GH #566 / ISS-0617 (docs/issues/ISS-0617.json, read the confirmed_root_cause field in full). Root cause: repository_artifacts is a GLOBAL_REGISTRY table (canonical home: public) whose tenant_default shadow copy was never dropped, because migration GBL-134's v_tables allow-list (migrations/GBL-134_iss0185_drop_global_registry_shadows.sql lines 45-70) contains only 24 of the 37 tables that docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml itself classifies as GLOBAL_REGISTRY. 13 are missing, including repository_artifacts (this issue's direct cause) plus api_token_audit, artifact_versions, event_payload_store, event_type_registry_producers, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, oidc_migration_item, oidc_migration_job, registry_idp_operation_ledger, tenant, tenant_hostnames, variable_schemas. GBL-134 has ALREADY RUN against multiple databases (confirmed: the shared bpm_test database, workspace r-co-2's bpm_dev) -- it cannot be edited in place; migrations in this repo's convention are immutable once applied. Your design must specify a NEW forward migration (following the same GBL-<NNN> naming convention and the same safety-guarded DROP TABLE pattern GBL-134 itself uses -- read that file in full for the pattern: existence checks before dropping, RESTRICT mode, per-tenant-schema loop) that completes the originally-intended 37-table GLOBAL_REGISTRY drop by covering the 13 missing names. IMPORTANT SEPARATE CONCERN YOU MUST ALSO ADDRESS: a DIFFERENT, more severe issue was found in the SAME migration during this diagnosis and has been filed separately as ISS-0620 / GH #573 (BLOCKER, potential data loss) -- GBL-134's v_tables list ALSO wrongly includes 4 tables (artifact_activation_groups, entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances) that the diagnosis actually classifies as PER_TENANT (opposite direction -- tenant_default should be canonical, not public), meaning those 4 have ALREADY been incorrectly dropped from tenant_default. Read docs/issues/ISS-0620.json for full detail. YOUR DESIGN FOR THIS ISSUE (GH-566/ISS-0617) MUST NOT ATTEMPT TO FIX ISS-0620'S PROBLEM -- that is out of scope for this run and has its own separate queued issue. But your new forward migration's table list MUST be constructed by cross-referencing the diagnosis file's global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray list directly (all 37 names) MINUS the 24 already in GBL-134's original list MINUS explicitly excluding the 4 misclassified names ISS-0620 identified (do not re-verify or re-decide ISS-0620's classification question -- simply exclude those 4 from your new migration's scope since they need separate handling under ISS-0620, not silent inclusion here). This means your new migration's table list should be exactly the 13 names: api_token_audit, artifact_versions, event_payload_store, event_type_registry_producers, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, oidc_migration_item, oidc_migration_job, registry_idp_operation_ledger, repository_artifacts, tenant, tenant_hostnames, variable_schemas. Read the full diagnosis file (docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml) and GBL-134's full source before designing.

REWORK 1:
- [BLOCKER] Section 5's core factual claim is backwards. Live inspection of bpm_test shows api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, and variable_schemas have ALREADY had their public copies dropped by GBL-135 (confirmed both by direct psql query returning 0 rows for all 5 in public, and by GBL-135's ACTUAL v_tables array -- not just its stale header comment -- containing all 5 names). The design asserts the opposite. Consequence: GBL-136's Defense 1 guard (only drop if table exists in public) will silently skip these 5 as no-ops, leaving their tenant_default shadows undropped -- directly contradicting the design's own Section 8 verification query. Rework options: (a) design a path to drop these 5 tables' tenant_default copies despite their public copies already being gone (relax/special-case Defense 1 for exactly these 5, with its own safety analysis), (b) explicitly exclude these 5 from GBL-136's scope with documented rationale, correcting the Section 8 verification query and the 13-name count accordingly, or (c) note the underlying double-classification conflict in the diagnosis file and pick the operationally-safe resolution GBL-135 already established (these 5 are PER_TENANT canonical, matching what GBL-135 already did) -- likely the correct answer is (b)/(c) combined: these 5 should NOT be in GBL-136's scope at all, since GBL-135 already resolved them in the opposite direction, meaning the true 'missing GLOBAL_REGISTRY' set is 8 tables (13 minus these 5), not 13. Re-verify this conclusion against source before finalizing.
- [MINOR] Section 3's FK table for artifact_versions is missing one dependent: tenant_default.repository_form_schemas.version_id -> artifact_versions (fk_form_schema_version). Add it for completeness (doesn't change the conclusion).
acceptance_criteria: Design specifies a NEW forward migration (not an edit to GBL-134) covering exactly the 13 missing GLOBAL_REGISTRY table names, explicitly excluding the 4 ISS-0620-flagged names
New migration follows GBL-134s own safety pattern (existence checks, RESTRICT, per-tenant-schema loop) -- design must show it read and understood that pattern, not invented a new one
Design explicitly states it does NOT attempt to resolve ISS-0620 in this run
Design explains how this fixes TC-EXP-601-01 through 04 (the repository_artifacts shadow removal unblocks the resolver JOIN)
No implementation code present in the design artefact (SQL migration content can be described precisely in prose/pseudocode per Type C/E convention, not as a literal runnable script)
